title: Statistics and cardinality estimation
description: Learn how SQL Server uses statistics objects to estimate row counts and choose efficient query plans.

data.text: Statistics are binary data objects that describe the distribution of column values in a table or index. The query optimizer uses these statistics to estimate how many rows a query will return. Accurate cardinality estimates are essential for choosing the right join type, join order, and whether to use an index seek or scan.

SQL Server automatically creates statistics on indexed columns. It also creates auto-created statistics on non-indexed columns when the query optimizer detects a predicate that would benefit from statistics. Each statistics object stores a histogram with up to 200 steps, plus density information for distinct column combinations.

data.title: List statistics for a table
data.content: Use this query to see which statistics objects exist on the Orders table and when they were last updated.
data.code:
SELECT
    s.name AS StatsName,
    s.auto_created,
    s.user_created,
    STATS_DATE(s.object_id, s.stats_id) AS LastUpdated
FROM sys.stats AS s
JOIN sys.tables AS t ON t.object_id = s.object_id
WHERE t.name = 'Orders';

data.text: The histogram divides column values into up to 200 steps. Each step records the upper bound value, the number of rows equal to that value, and the number of rows less than that value. Density measures the uniqueness of column combinations and is used for equality predicates when the histogram does not provide a good estimate.

data.title: Common causes of bad estimates
items: Out-of-date statistics after large data loads or deletes
Ascending key problems where new values are always above the histogram maximum
Correlated columns where single-column statistics do not capture the true relationship

data.title: Update statistics with a full scan
data.content: A full scan ensures the histogram is built from all rows, giving the most accurate distribution.

data.title: Auto-update thresholds can be misleading
data.text: By default, SQL Server updates statistics when table row counts change by 20 percent plus 500 rows. A table with 1 million rows may not update until 200,500 rows change. For volatile tables, manual or scheduled updates are often better.

data.title: Takeaway
points: Statistics describe data distribution using histograms and density
Cardinality estimates drive plan choices for joins, indexes, and parallelism
Out-of-date statistics are a common cause of slow plans
Full scans and filtered statistics can fix estimate problems
data.takeaway: Good statistics are the foundation of good query plans. Monitor update age and consider custom update strategies for high-volatility tables.
